back: Slavery in which the person is property, can be sold at any time and passes slave status to the children.
Slavery within a household or community; enslaved people often had some rights and their descendants could be absorbed into the family.
Handing over a person as security for a debt; the pawn could be enslaved if the debt was not repaid.

front: What goods went south across the Sahara in exchange for gold and captives?
back: Salt, horses, cloth and metal goods.

front: What created new demand for captives in nineteenth-century East Africa?
back: The clove plantations of Zanzibar and Pemba and the sugar islands of the Indian Ocean.
Captives were sold for guns; guns made it easier to take more captives; threatened neighbours had to join in to get guns themselves.

front: Give one economic, one social and one political cause of the slave trade.
back: Economic: demand for plantation labour. Social: debt or punishment for crimes. Political: wars between states.

front: Name five methods of obtaining slaves.
back: Raids, wars, kidnapping, debt or pawnship, punishment for crimes (also trade at markets and tribute).

front: How did most Europeans on the West African coast obtain captives?
back: They bought them from African rulers and merchants at coastal forts and markets; European demand drove the trade.
